title: AI poses uneven opportunities and risks across APAC cities
gist: Oxford Economics says AI will boost electronics-manufacturing and service-centric Asia Pacific cities while posing labour risks to outsourcing hubs like Manila and Bengaluru and widening regional inequality.

insights.claim: Professional-services gross value added has grown an average 7.9% per year since 2000 across Oxford's Asia Pacific cities, underpinning their rise as economic hubs.
insights.speaker: Jiawen Cui
insights.so_what: Services strength is the base AI could reinforce.

insights.claim: AI-related exports are set to boom across Asia this year, supporting strong manufacturing growth in Hsinchu (Taiwan), Georgetown (Malaysia) and Hai Phong (Vietnam).
insights.speaker: Jiawen Cui
insights.so_what: AI hardware supply-chain nodes in Taiwan, Malaysia and Vietnam are regional beneficiaries.
insights.locator: Cities that cater to AI-related demand

insights.claim: As AI adoption rises, service-centric hubs such as Singapore, Beijing and Tokyo benefit most because IT and finance can best leverage the technology for productivity and income gains.
insights.speaker: Jiawen Cui
insights.so_what: AI productivity gains accrue to financial and IT service hubs.

insights.claim: Oxford does not expect widespread job losses from AI but sees greater exposure in low value-added ICT and administrative roles, raising risk for outsourcing economies like Manila and Bengaluru and widening inequality as rural and industrial regions fall behind.
insights.speaker: Jiawen Cui
insights.so_what: Philippine BPO and Indian IT-services cities are the exposed nodes.
